query: What is the current state of polling and political dynamics for Zambia's August 2026 presidential election, specifically Hakainde Hichilema's expected vote share? Include recent 2025-2026 polls, opposition coalition strength, whether Edgar Lungu/PF is running (note Lungu died in 2025), and turnout factors.
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings on Zambia's August 2026 presidential election:

## Bottom Line

**Hakainde Hichilema (UPND) is the clear frontrunner**, with credible indicators pointing to a likely first-round majority in the **55–63% range**. The key dynamics:

**Polling (with quality caveats — Zambia lacks rigorous independent polling):**
- **Most credible source** (academic Zambia Election Research Network survey, fieldwork Jun–Nov 2025): **55% for Hichilema vs 13% opposition**, with ~32% undecided
- **Dr. Mutombo/UNZA national poll** (Dec 2025): **60%** (58–63% range) vs 35% opposition; 75% approval
- Opposition claims of "Mundubile 70%" are partisan projections, not neutral data

**Lungu/PF status:** Edgar Lungu **died 5 June 2025** in Pretoria. The PF is **NOT running as a unified party** — it fractured into competing camps. The opposition regrouped under the **Tonse Pamodzi Alliance**, which selected **Brian Mundubile** as candidate in January 2026. Lungu had also been disqualified by the Constitutional Court before his death.

**Opposition coalition:** Weak and fragmented. It's a "negative coalition" of 20+ factions; 14 candidates split the anti-incumbent vote; the alliance failed to field parliamentary candidates in ~75 of 226 constituencies.

**Turnout factors:** Cost of living is the central issue and the main downside risk for Hichilema. Geography favors him (strong in Southern/Western/North-Western; opposition strong in Luapula/Northern/Muchinga/Eastern). Analysts flag democratic-backsliding concerns (alleged capture of the PF, police blocking opposition rallies).

The full structured findings, data points, and sources have been recorded.

key_facts: Zambia's general election is scheduled for 13 August 2026 (president, National Assembly, councillors, council chairs); a presidential candidate needs 50%+1 to avoid a runoff.
Incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema (UPND) is seeking a second term; he won the 2021 election with 59.02% of the vote.
Former President Edgar Lungu (PF, president 2015-2021) died on 5 June 2025 in Pretoria, South Africa, from surgery complications.

The Patriotic Front (PF) is NOT running as a unified party — it fractured into competing camps (Sampa, Lubinda, Chabinga); Lungu had also been disqualified by the Constitutional Court before his death.

Brian Mundubile (PF Mporokoso MP) was elected Tonse Pamodzi Alliance presidential candidate on 28 January 2026, defeating Danny Pule 129-34; his running mate is Makebi Zulu (Lungu family spokesperson).
14 presidential candidates were cleared by the ECZ (~1 July 2026), but it is effectively a two-horse race between Hichilema and Mundubile.
The most credible poll (Zambia Election Research Network / academic, fieldwork Jun-Nov 2025) found 55% voting intention for Hichilema vs 13% for the fragmented opposition, with ~32% undecided.
A December 2025 national poll supervised by UNZA demographer Dr. Namuunda Mutombo put Hichilema at 60% (range 58-63%) vs 35% opposition, with a 75% approval rating.
Opposition/Tonse Alliance figures (Chris Zumani Zimba) claim Mundubile will win 70%+ in the first round, but this is a partisan projection unsupported by neutral polling.
Registered voters total ~8.79-8.86 million (ECZ certified roll: 8,861,918); largest blocs are Lusaka (1,430,889), Copperbelt (1,296,446), and Eastern (1,129,444).
The Tonse Alliance failed to field parliamentary candidates in roughly 75 of 226 constituencies, weakening grassroots turnout capacity.

Cost of living is the dominant issue; government claims inflation fell from 24% (Aug 2021) to 6.5% (Jun 2026) and 94% of sovereign debt restructured, while voter economic sentiment is split (41% worse, 38% better).
Hichilema's strongholds are Southern, Western, and North-Western provinces (plus Central); opposition strongholds are Luapula, Northern, Muchinga, Eastern, and parts of Copperbelt/Lusaka.
Analysts (ISS, Mail & Guardian, BTI 2026) allege a tilted playing field: UPND capture of the opposition PF, police blocking opposition assemblies, and electoral irregularities.

In the academic survey, 51% expected free and fair elections (62% of UPND supporters vs 36% of opposition supporters); 70% did not fear for their safety; only 33% planned to re-elect their MP and 15% their councillor.
